title: 第54章西大陆的海岸第56章 钢铁城的传闻
lines: 残破木船破开滞涩的黑海海面，持续向西匀速滑行，船体破损带来的轻微倾斜贯穿全程，每一次浪涌起伏都带着不对称的硬质钝压，持续传导至甲板每一处角落，让所有人的躯体始终处于微失衡的紧绷状态。风暴过后的海面依旧笼罩在厚重灰雾之下，天光惨白稀薄，无任何温热落点，无边无际的暗沉水域反复堆叠着单调、荒芜、死寂的远洋氛围，时间失去刻度，只剩机械往复的航行颠簸与海风削耳的细碎声响，层层叠叠压榨着人的神经与体能。

连续四日跨海续航，海域景致从未出现半分生机，唯有周遭环境的体感在缓慢且持续地异变，无声昭示着距离西大陆疆域越来越近。原本纯净的海风湿涩感逐渐浑浊，裹挟的气息愈发驳杂，深海土霉死水味持续加重，混杂着厚重的油污腐臭味、持续弥散的辐射灼烧焦糊味，还有一丝淡到极致、若有若无的铁腥气，不是新鲜血液的浓烈，是长期锈蚀、腐烂、坏死肌理沉淀的陈旧腥腐味，死死黏附在衣料、皮肤、呼吸道表层，每一次呼吸都带着气管磨砂般的涩痛，胸腔闷胀压抑，生理性的不适感连绵不绝。
海面水体也彻底褪去东陆近海的暗沉通透，化作浓稠浑浊的灰黑色，表层漂浮着细碎的油垢薄膜与辐射尘碎屑，浪纹涌动时会泛起黏腻的波光，水波破碎的瞬间发出滞涩的闷响，没有清脆水声，只有死水蠕动的厚重钝感。船体破开海面的阻力持续变大，水流黏滞厚重，每一次前行都要强行撕开浓稠水体，船速肉眼可见地放缓，无形的阻滞感层层堆叠，压得整艘孤船愈发沉坠。
胸口十字徽章的低频钝灼感持续加剧，皮肉发麻的范围从胸腔蔓延至脖颈、下颌与整条手臂，不再是遥远能量场的微弱共振，而是近距离紊乱戾气的持续渗透，钝痛沉涩、顽固不散，没有尖锐预警，只有深入肌理的持续不适感，时刻提醒着前方疆域的秩序崩塌与能量失控。视野远端的雾层灰度持续加深，辐射干扰愈发强烈，视线边缘始终覆着一层洗不掉的灰翳，视物轻微失真、重叠、模糊，是西陆全域辐射紊乱最直观的体感征兆。
甲板众人的疲态随航程推进不断累加，所有人依旧维持着本能的紧绷体态，无一人敢松懈神经。废土远洋的规则直白残酷，海域异变即是凶险前置，越是靠近未知大陆，越不能暴露半分破绽，松弛即是覆灭。

陆寻立身船舵侧方，躯体微微前倾，肩背肌群全程僵硬酸胀，没有片刻舒展。掌心包扎的纱布被海风与湿气浸透，微微发硬，创口位置持续传来闷沉的钝痛，细微发力便会牵扯整片掌面肌理，涩痛感顺着手臂蔓延至肩背。腰背旧伤的隐痛反复拉扯，四肢皮层被西陆近海的辐射气流侵蚀，通体发麻、滞涩、发凉。他眼底沉黑无半分光亮，情绪尽数封存克制，无前路忐忑、无初见忐忑、无疲惫倦怠，只剩底层求生者极致审慎的观测与预判，呼吸匀冷恒定，节律刻板规整，全程紧盯前方雾海深处，捕捉每一处细微异动。
苏野伫立船头，骨骼肌群从肩背到脚踝完全锁死，厮杀本能始终处于高位运转状态。旧伤肌理的撕裂痛感不间断侵蚀神经，他却无半点神态波动，眼神死锁前方浓雾，瞳孔凝缩成细窄黑线，视野扫过海面每一处漂浮残骸、每一缕异动雾流、每一寸浑浊水体，无一处遗漏、无一处松懈。他早已适应这种长久的静默戒备，乱世之中，所有安稳都是假象，唯有极致警惕才能守住生机。

林小满静立陆寻身侧，眉心始终紧蹙成无法舒展的僵硬褶皱，精神感知系统持续过载。西陆弥散的紊乱能量疯狂穿刺、拉扯、磨损她的精神丝线，颅腔深处的钝痛层层加重，比远洋海域更为剧烈，视野灰翳愈发厚重，偶尔会出现短暂的视野失焦。她呼吸浅促细碎，胸廓起伏微弱，单薄躯体不受控地出现细微震颤，脆弱的感知锚点持续预警着前方疆域的极度凶险，无间断的精神消耗让她面色愈发苍白，疲态尽数外露，却始终咬牙稳住感知，不肯有半分松懈。
船员各司其职，动作愈发机械滞缓，四日不间断的航行修整、精神紧绷、体能消耗，让每个人的肌理都堆满透支的破绽。掌心勒痕发硬、指尖泛白僵硬、面色惨白无血色，无人言语、无人喘息、无人抱怨，只靠着绝境求生的本能持续作业，把控船舵、监测风向、排查船体、观望前路，维持船只的平稳续航。
雾层愈发浓稠，海天边界彻底消融，整片天地沦为一体的暗沉灰蒙，视野被压缩至不足百米，前方景致彻底模糊，未知感与压抑感无限放大。浓稠的雾气带着刺骨冷涩的湿凉，裹挟各类腐浊气息反复冲刷甲板，皮层发麻、发僵、发冷，生理性的窒息感持续堆叠，将整艘孤船彻底包裹在荒芜死寂的氛围之中。
风缓。
水滞。
天光彻底凝滞。
极致的静态留白铺展数分钟，耳膜空鸣的低频震颤覆盖所有听觉，天地间无任何动态声响，死寂压覆一切，酝酿着即将揭晓的全新疆域。
最先突破雾层遮挡的，是一截扭曲锈蚀的金属轮廓。
它从灰雾深处缓慢浮现，锈迹厚重、形态狰狞，断裂的金属构架歪扭弯折，半截裸露在海面之上，半截沉在浑浊水下，表层覆盖着油泥与辐射尘，海水冲刷的痕迹狰狞斑驳，是旧时代文明崩塌后遗留的残骸，死寂伫立，无人问津，在雾中透出冰冷的破败感。
紧接着，更多残骸陆续浮现。
断裂的船体骨架、破碎的机械零件、坍塌的建材残块、扭曲的钢筋铁皮，无数文明碎片杂乱堆砌在近海海域，层层叠叠、密密麻麻，将整片浅海区域铺成一片废墟坟场。浑浊海水反复冲刷残骸缝隙，裹挟着腐烂杂质与辐射污泥，每一次浪涌都翻涌出更浓重的土霉、油污与焦糊混杂的恶浊气息，扑面而来，呛得人胸腔涩痛加剧。
雾层缓缓散开，视野逐步开阔。
西大陆的海岸，彻底展露在众人眼前。
没有规整岸线、没有平整滩涂、没有生机绿意、没有人居烟火，整片海岸绵延至视野尽头，尽数是黑褐色的焦枯滩地，土质硬化皲裂，表层覆盖着一层薄薄的辐射灰垢与油泥结块，踩踏即碎，碎屑随风飘散。海岸线之上无半分完整植被，所有草木尽数枯死、碳化、倒伏，枝干扭曲发黑，杂乱堆砌在滩地之上，如同无数枯骨陈列，荒凉且狰狞。
近海沿岸错落分布着大片坍塌废墟，旧时代建筑的混凝土墙体断裂倾斜，钢筋裸露锈蚀，楼层塌陷镂空，窗洞漆黑空洞，如同无数双死寂的眼窝，空洞地望向茫茫海域。整片废墟群连绵起伏，覆盖整条海岸带，无一处完整建筑、无一处规整格局、无一处活着的文明痕迹，只剩崩塌、腐朽、荒芜的死寂图景。

The broken wooden ship broke through the stagnant surface of the Black Sea and continued to glide westward at a constant speed. The slight inclination caused by the damage to the hull ran throughout the entire process. Every surge and rise brought an asymmetrical hard blunt pressure, which continued to be transmitted to every corner of the deck, keeping everyone's bodies in a slightly unbalanced and tense state. The sea surface after the storm is still shrouded in thick gray fog. The sky is pale and thin, without any warmth. The endless dark waters are repeatedly filled with a monotonous, desolate, and dead ocean atmosphere. Time has lost its scale, and only the bumps of the mechanical reciprocating voyage and the tinny sound of the sea breeze are left, layer upon layer squeezing people's nerves and physical energy.
After sailing across the sea for four consecutive days, the sea scenery never showed any signs of life. Only the physical sensation of the surrounding environment was slowly and continuously changing, silently indicating that the territory of the Western Continent was getting closer and closer. The originally pure sea breeze's moist and astringent feeling gradually became turbid, and the enveloping smell became more and more complex. The smell of deep-sea earthy mold and stagnant water continued to increase, mixed with the thick rotten smell of oil, the persistent and diffuse smell of radiation burning, and a trace of extremely light and vague iron smell, wasn't it? The strong smell of fresh blood is an old fishy smell accumulated from long-term rust, rot, and necrotic texture. It clings to the surface of clothing, skin, and respiratory tract. Every breath brings a grinding pain in the trachea, the chest is bloated and depressed, and the physiological discomfort is endless.
The sea surface water has also completely lost the darkness and transparency of the East China Sea, turning into a thick and turbid gray-black. There are fine films of oil dirt and radioactive dust debris floating on the surface. When the waves surge, there will be sticky waves. When the water waves break, there will be a dull and muffled sound. There is no crisp sound of water, only the thick and dull feeling of stagnant water. The resistance of the ship's hull breaking through the sea surface continues to increase, and the current is viscous and thick. Every time it moves forward, the thick water must be forcibly torn apart. The ship's speed slows down visibly to the naked eye. Invisible stagnation piles up layer by layer, making the entire lonely ship sink more and more.
The low-frequency dull burning sensation on the cross badge on the chest continued to intensify, and the numbness spread from the chest to the neck, jaw, and entire arms. It was no longer the weak resonance of the distant energy field, but the continuous penetration of chaotic and violent energy at close range. The dull pain was deep and stubborn. There was no sharp warning, only the continuous discomfort that penetrated into the texture, constantly reminding the front territory of the collapse of order and loss of energy. The grayscale of the fog layer at the far end of the field of vision continues to deepen, and the radiation interference becomes more and more intense. The edge of the field of vision is always covered with a layer of gray haze that cannot be washed away. The visual objects are slightly distorted, overlapping, and blurred. This is the most intuitive somatosensory sign of radiation disorder in the entire Western Continent.
The fatigue of everyone on the deck continued to accumulate as the voyage progressed. Everyone still maintained their instinctive tense posture, and no one dared to relax their nerves. The rules of the wasteland and ocean are straightforward and cruel. Changes in the sea area are dangers. The closer you get to the unknown continent, the less you can expose any flaws. Relaxation means destruction.
Lu Xun stood on the side of the rudder, leaning forward slightly. The muscles in his shoulders and back were stiff and sore throughout, without a moment of relaxation. The gauze covering the palm was soaked by the sea breeze and moisture, and became slightly hard. A dull dull pain continued to be felt at the wound site. The slightest exertion of force would pull the entire palm texture, and the aching pain spread along the arm to the shoulder and back. The dull pain from an old injury in the lower back pulls repeatedly, and the cortex of the limbs is eroded by the radiant airflow from the western continent and offshore, leaving the whole body numb, stagnant, and cold. His eyes were dark and without any light, and all his emotions were sealed and restrained. There was no fear of the future, no fear of the first sight, and no fatigue. All that remained was the extremely prudent observation and prediction of a bottom-level survivor. His breathing was even and steady, and his rhythm was rigid and regular. He stared at the depths of the sea of ​​fog in front of him throughout the whole process, capturing every slight movement.
Su Ye stood at the bow of the boat, his skeletal muscles completely locked from his shoulders and back to his ankles, and his fighting instinct was always operating at a high level. The tearing pain of the old injury's texture continued to erode his nerves, but he did not have any fluctuations in his expression. His eyes were locked on the thick fog in front of him, and his pupils were condensed into thin black lines. His vision swept across every floating wreckage on the sea surface, every wisp of abnormal fog, and every inch of turbid water. No one was missed or slackened. He has long been accustomed to this long-term silent vigilance. In troubled times, all stability is an illusion, and only extreme vigilance can keep the chance of survival.
Lin Xiaoman stood quietly beside Lu Xun, his eyebrows always furrowed into stiff folds that could not be stretched, and his mental perception system continued to be overloaded. The chaotic energy dispersed in the Western Continent crazily pierced, pulled, and worn away her spiritual threads. The dull pain deep in the skull cavity became more severe, more severe than in the ocean. The gray haze in her vision became thicker and thicker, and occasionally there would be brief out-of-focus vision. Her breathing was shallow and broken, her chest rose and fell weakly, her thin body trembled uncontrollably, and her fragile sensory anchor continued to warn of the extremely dangerous territory ahead. The constant mental consumption made her face paler and her exhaustion was exposed, but she always gritted her teeth to stabilize her perception and refused to relax even a little bit.
The crew performed their duties, and their movements became increasingly sluggish. The four days of non-stop sailing and repairs, mental stress, and physical exertion left everyone's skin full of overdraft flaws. The palms were hard with cuts, the fingertips were white and stiff, and the face was pale and bloodless. No one spoke, no one breathed, no one complained. They only relied on the instinct of survival in desperate situations to continue working, controlling the rudder, monitoring the wind direction, checking the hull, and watching the way forward to maintain the smooth sailing of the ship.
The fog layer became thicker and thicker, the boundary between sea and sky completely melted, and the whole world became one dark gray. The field of vision was compressed to less than a hundred meters, the scenery ahead was completely blurred, and the sense of unknown and depression was infinitely magnified. The thick mist carried biting and cold dampness, carrying various rotten smells and washing over the deck repeatedly. The skin was numb, stiff, and cold, and the physiological suffocation continued to pile up, completely wrapping the entire solitary ship in a desolate and dead atmosphere.
The wind is gentle.
Water stagnation.
The skylight completely froze.
The ultimate static blankness spreads for several minutes, and the low-frequency vibration of eardrums covers all hearing. There is no dynamic sound between heaven and earth. Deathly silence overwhelms everything, brewing a new territory that is about to be revealed.
The first thing to break through the fog layer was a twisted and corroded metal outline.
It emerged slowly from the depths of the gray fog, with thick rust and a hideous shape. The broken metal frame was twisted and twisted, half exposed above the sea surface, and half sunk under the turbid water. The surface was covered with oil sludge and radioactive dust, and the traces of seawater erosion were hideous and mottled. It was the remains left after the collapse of the civilization of the old era. It stood dead and silent, with no one caring about it, and a cold sense of dilapidation was revealed in the fog.
Immediately afterwards, more wreckage emerged one after another.
Broken hull frames, shattered mechanical parts, collapsed building materials, twisted steel sheets, and countless fragments of civilization were piled up in the offshore waters, layer upon layer, densely packed, turning the entire shallow sea area into a cemetery of ruins. The turbid seawater repeatedly washed away the gaps in the wreckage, enveloping rotten impurities and radiation sludge. With each surge, a thicker and turbid smell of earth mold, oil stains and burnt mixture rushed out, rushing towards the face, making the chest pain intensify.
The fog layer slowly dispersed, and the field of vision gradually broadened.
The coast of the Western Continent is completely exposed to everyone.
There is no regular coastline, no flat tidal flats, no lively greenery, and no residential fireworks. The entire coast stretches to the end of the field of vision, and is filled with dark brown scorched beach land. The soil is hardened and cracked, and the surface is covered with a thin layer of radiation ash and oily sludge. It breaks into pieces when stepped on, and the debris is blown away by the wind. There is no complete vegetation on the coastline. All the vegetation is dead, carbonized, and lodging, and the branches are twisted and blackened. They are piled on the beach in disorder, like countless dead bones, desolate and hideous.
Large areas of collapsed ruins are scattered along the coast. The concrete walls of old-era buildings are broken and tilted, the steel bars are exposed and corroded, the floors are collapsed and hollow, and the window holes are dark and empty, like countless pairs of dead eye sockets, looking blankly into the vast sea. The entire group of ruins is rolling up and down, covering the entire coastal zone. There is no complete building, no regular pattern, no trace of living civilization, only a dead scene of collapse, decay, and desolation.
